assertions.quote: M. avium complex is the most common cause of NTM infections in humans, and the respiratory system is the most common site of infection.

assertions.subject: Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis
assertions.quote: M. avium subspecies paratuberculosis was identified in ruminants as a causative agent for Johne disease.

assertions.subject: Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis
assertions.quote: Some have hypothesized and debated for decades that M. avium subspecies paratuberculosis is the etiological agent of Crohn disease in humans without strong evidence.

assertions.subject: Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis
assertions.quote: A recent publication found a high prevalence of M. avium subspecies paratuberculosis antibodies in inflammatory bowel diseases when compared to patients with noninflammatory bowel diseases, 64% vs. 9.7%.

assertions.subject: Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis
assertions.quote: M. avium subspecies paratuberculosis has also been reported to trigger autoimmunity, including multiple sclerosis and type 1 diabetes mellitus.
